title: Mattresses From India: Preliminary Results and Rescission, in Part, of Antidumping Duty Administrative Review; 2024-2025
abstract: The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) preliminarily determines that producers/exporters subject to this review made sales of subject merchandise at less than normal value (NV) during the period of review (POR), March 1, 2024, through August 31, 2025. In addition, we are rescinding the review with respect to four companies. Interested parties are invited to comment on these preliminary results of review.

title: Certain New Pneumatic Off-the-Road Tires From India: Final Results of Antidumping Duty Administrative Review; 2024-2025
abstract: The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) determines that certain producers/exporters subject to this review made sales of subject merchandise at less than normal value (NV) during the period of review (POR), March 1, 2024, through February 28, 2025.

title: Petition for Rulemaking To Consider Amendments to Regulations Governing Interim Use of Rights-of-Way as Trails
abstract: The Board partially grants a petition for rulemaking and proposes amendments to its regulations implementing section 208 of the National Trails System Act Amendments of 1983 to streamline the railbanking process. Under the proposal, the Board would no longer issue Notices or Certificates of Interim Trail Use during trail-use negotiations. Only after an agreement is reached would the Board issue an order authorizing transfer to the trail sponsor. Abandonment authority would no longer be prerequisite to railbanking. The Board would also confirm that by authorizing transfer the Board is not exercising any power of eminent domain or authorizing a taking.

title: Prestressed Concrete Steel Wire Strand From the People's Republic of China: Continuation of Antidumping Duty and Countervailing Duty Orders
abstract: As a result of the determinations by the U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) and the U.S. International Trade Commission (ITC) that revocation of the antidumping duty (AD) and countervailing duty (CVD) orders on prestressed concrete steel wire strand (PC strand) from the People's Republic of China (China) would likely lead to the continuation or recurrence of dumping, countervailable subsidies, and material injury to an industry in the United States, Commerce is publishing a notice of continuation of these AD and CVD orders.

title: Certain Pea Protein From the People's Republic of China: Preliminary Results, Partial Rescission, and Preliminary Determination of No Shipments of Antidumping Duty Administrative Review; 2023-2025; Correction
abstract: The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) published notice in the Federal Register on November 16, 2026, in which Commerce announced the preliminary results of the 2023-2025 administrative review of the antidumping duty (AD) order on certain pea protein (pea protein) from the People's Republic of China (China). This notice incorrectly listed the preliminary weighted-average dumping margin (percent) for Yantai T.Full Biotech Co., Ltd. and the non-individually examined companies receiving a separate rate which include Bioway Industrial Group Ltd., Linyi Yuwang Vegetable Protein Co., Ltd., and Yosin Biotechnology (Yantai) Co., Ltd.

title: Tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane From the People's Republic of China: Preliminary Affirmative Determination of Sales at Less Than Fair Value, Postponement of Final Determination and Extension of Provisional Measures
abstract: The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) preliminarily determines that Tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane (Tris) from the People's Republic of China (China) is being, or is likely to be, sold in the United States at less than fair value (LTFV). The period of investigation (POI) is October 1, 2025, through March 31, 2026. Interested parties are invited to comment on this preliminary determination.

title: Request for Comments Regarding International Trade Commission's Economic Analysis
abstract: Pursuant to Section 332 of the Tariff Act of 1930, the United States International Trade Commission (Commission) is seeking information from the public on its economic analysis, including its methodology and areas of focus.

title: Combined Notice of Filings #1
Establishment of Class E Airspace; Trading Bay Production Airport, Trading Bay, AK
abstract: This action establishes Class E airspace extending upward from 700 feet above the surface at Trading Bay Production Airport, Trading Bay, AK. This action supports the safety and management of instrument flight rules (IFR) operations at the airport.

title: Auction of Flexible-Use Licenses in the Upper C-Band for Next-Generation Wireless Services; Notice and Filing Requirements, Minimum Opening Bids, Upfront Payments, and Other Procedures for Auction 115; Bidding Scheduled To Begin April 27, 2027
abstract: This document summarizes the procedures, deadlines, upfront payment, and minimum opening bid amounts adopted in the Auction 115 Procedures Public Notice for the Federal Communications Commission's (Commission) upcoming auction of 3,248 new flexible-use licenses in the 3.98-4.14 GHz portion of the Upper C-band. The Auction 115 Procedures Public Notice summarized here provides details regarding the procedures, terms, conditions, dates, and deadlines governing participation in Auction 115 bidding, as well as an overview of the post-auction application and payment processes.

title: Additions to the Entity List
abstract: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by adding 7 entities to the Entity List, under the destinations of Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand. These entities have been determined by the U.S. Government to be acting contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States.

title: Supervisory Committee Audits And Verifications
abstract: The NCUA Board (Board) is amending its regulations governing supervisory committee audits to eliminate unnecessary, redundant, and overly prescriptive provisions. The final rule is necessary to reduce regulatory burden, increase operational flexibility for federally insured credit unions (FICUs), and streamline the rules by removing requirements that are outdated or duplicative of other authorities. The intended effect of the final rule is to simplify compliance for FICUs without compromising the integrity of the audit process.

title: Corporate Credit Unions
abstract: The NCUA Board (Board) is amending its regulations for corporate credit unions by removing the requirement that a corporate credit union's asset and liability management committee (ALCO) must have at least one member who is also a member of the corporate credit union's board of directors. The final rule also removes filing requirements related to a corporate credit union's annual report and any management letter or other report issued by its independent public accountant. The intended effect is to reduce unnecessary regulatory burden and provide corporate credit unions with greater flexibility.

title: Thresholds Increase for the Major Assets Prohibition of the Depository Institution Management Interlocks Act Rule
abstract: The NCUA Board (Board) is issuing a final rule increasing two thresholds in its regulation implementing management official interlocks for purposes of the Depository Institution Management Interlocks Act (DIMIA). DIMIA authorizes NCUA to adjust the major assets prohibition thresholds through regulation to respond to inflation or market changes. This final rule increases both major assets prohibition thresholds to $10 billion to account for changes in the United States banking market since 1996. Additionally, the final rule removes a presumption related to depository institutions controlled or managed by persons who are members of a minority group or women.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Revision of an Approved Information Collection; Comment Request; Company-Run Annual Stress Test Reporting Template and Documentation for Covered Institutions With Total Consolidated Assets of $250 Billion or More Under the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act
abstract: The OCC, as part of its continuing effort to reduce paperwork and respondent burden, invites comment on a continuing information collection, as required by the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA). In accordance with the requirements of the PRA, the OCC may not conduct or sponsor, and the respondent is not required to respond to, an information collection unless it displays a currently valid Office of Management and Budget (OMB) control number. The OCC is soliciting comment concerning a revision to its information collection titled "Company-Run Annual Stress Test Reporting Template and Documentation for Covered Institutions with Total Consolidated Assets of $250 Billion or More under the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act."

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for the Rio Grande Shiner
abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the Rio Grande shiner (Notropis jemezanus), a fish species from the Rio Grande Basin in New Mexico, Texas, and Mexico, as an endangered species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the Rio Grande shiner. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. We find that critical habitat for this species is not determinable at this time.

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for Peppered Shiner
abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the peppered shiner (Miniellus perpallidus), a fish species from southeast Oklahoma and southern Arkansas, as an endangered species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the peppered shiner. After a review of the best available scientific and commercial information, we find that listing the species is warranted. Accordingly, we propose to list the peppered shiner as an endangered species under the Act. If finalized as proposed, this rule would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species.

title: Medicare Program; Contract Year 2028 Policy and Technical Changes to the Medicare Advantage Program, Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program, and Programs of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly

title: Restructuring the Governance and Funding Model of the Consolidated Audit Trail
abstract: Although the consolidated audit trail (the "CAT") continues to be a necessary regulatory tool, its decentralized governance has presented certain challenges to administering the CAT. To address those shortcomings, the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "Commission" or the "SEC") proposes to assume direct control of the CAT. Specifically, the Commission is proposing amendments to Regulation NMS under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 ("Exchange Act") that would rescind Rule 613, which obligates the national securities exchanges and national securities associations (collectively, the "SROs") to act jointly to develop a national market system plan to develop, implement, and maintain the CAT (the "CAT NMS Plan"). The Commission is simultaneously proposing new Rule 17a-26, which would require the SROs and broker-dealers to record and electronically report to a central repository substantially the same information that was previously required to be recorded and reported pursuant to Rule 613, the CAT NMS Plan, related SRO compliance rules, and related exemptive relief previously issued by the Commission.

title: Foreign-Trade Zone Subzone 21; Application for Subzone Expansion; DMA Industries, LLC; Mullins, South Carolina
Foreign-Trade Zone 143; Application for Subzone; Peak Energy Technologies Inc.; Sacramento, California
Loyalty and the Exclusive Purpose Rule in Selecting Plan Investments and Exercising Shareholder Rights
abstract: In this proposed rule, the Department of Labor (Department) clarifies the fiduciary duty of loyalty under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA). The proposed rule affirms that ERISA's duty of loyalty requires fiduciaries to act with the exclusive purpose of ensuring retirement security and providing promised benefits to plan participants and their beneficiaries. The amendments clarify the neutral application of ERISA's fiduciary duties of prudence and loyalty to selecting investments and investment courses of action, and to exercising shareholder rights, including proxy voting, the use of written proxy voting policies and guidelines, and shareholder engagement activities. The amendments would enhance the regulation by adding an affirmative expression of the duty of loyalty that is more consistent with the statute, and removing the tiebreaker test and participant preference provisions, which do not comport with the best reading of the statute and are susceptible to abuse, including use by a fiduciary as pretext to employ plan assets to pursue personal preferences or objectives unrelated to financial benefits under the plan. In the Department's view, the best reading of ERISA's exclusive purpose provision is and has always been that a plan fiduciary may not start with an ulterior motive or consider any factors collateral to plan participants' financial interests during any part of the process of making investment-selection decisions. The proposal would strengthen the fiduciary standards of pension and retirement plans covered by ERISA as instructed in President Trump's Executive Order 14366, Protecting American Investors from Foreign-Owned and Politically Motivated Proxy Advisors.

abstract: The Department of the Interior (DOI or Department), through Marine Minerals Administration (MMA), is incorporating by reference a collection of production measurement industry standards and safety industry standards into its regulations governing oil, gas, and sulfur operations on the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS). title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Threatened Species Status With Section 4(d) Rule for White Sands Pupfish and Critical Habitat Determination
abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the White Sands pupfish (Cyprinodon tularosa), a fish species from southcentral New Mexico, as a threatened species with protective regulations under section 4(d) of the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the White Sands pupfish. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. All areas meeting the definition of critical habitat for the White Sands pupfish occur on Department of War (DoW) owned facilities and are exempt from designation as critical habitat in accordance with section 4(a)(3)(B) of the Act. Therefore, we are not proposing any areas as critical habitat for the White Sands pupfish.

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for Mazama Newt
abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the Mazama newt (Taricha granulosa mazamae), an amphibian species from the Crater Lake caldera in Crater Lake National Park in Klamath County, Oregon, as an endangered species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the Mazama newt. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. We find that designating critical habitat for this species is not determinable at this time.

title: Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors
abstract: In this interim final rule (IFR), the Department of Commerce is establishing new rules to prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on U.S. technology to threaten U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. First, this rule establishes new restrictions which will apply for exports, reexports, or transfers (in-country) to overseas data centers that remotely supply significant volumes of compute to companies headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau. These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models. Data centers, foreign foundries, and chip exporters are required to perform robust due diligence on their customers, including any direct or indirect ownership or control by persons in Country Group D:5 or Macau, as part of complying with this new control. The license requirement will not apply to commercial recommender systems, such as those used by online retailers or social media companies, as these functions do not pose the same national security threat. Second, in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil (and any additional country designated by the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of State or the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs)--countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion. The license requirement for these five countries will not apply to semiconductors destined to companies headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent company is headquartered in, the United States, provided certain reporting requirements are met. Commerce will be actively monitoring for countries that tolerate evasion of this IFR and will consider a range of consequences for such countries, such as import restrictions, new license requirements on advanced semiconductor exports, downgrading the country's status in the U.S. export control regime, and Entity List designations and temporary export prohibitions for foreign persons involved in such activities. Third, this IFR amends the presumptions which front-end chips fabricators and chip packagers face when exporting advanced-node logic chips. These amendments reduce the number of pathways to overcome the presumptions for chip designers located in destinations which face a license requirement for SI chips. This change gives the U.S. government critical oversight over companies headquartered in certain countries that seek to leverage advanced semiconductor production capabilities in third countries. Finally, the IFR formally rescinds the regulations implementing the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule. The AI Diffusion Rule has never been enforced. The regulatory changes in this rule formalize the rescission of the AI Diffusion Rule, which the Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced in May 2025.

title: Certain Softwood Lumber Products From Canada: Amended Final Results of Countervailing Duty Administrative Review; 2024
abstract: The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) is amending the final results of the administrative review of the countervailing duty (CVD) order on certain softwood lumber products (softwood lumber) from Canada to correct a ministerial error. The period of review (POR) is January 1, 2024, through December 31, 2024.

abstract: This proposed rule would revise provisions regarding provider enrollment, medical review, investigations, and other program integrity oversight provisions to greatly strengthen our ability to crush fraud, enhance program integrity efforts across Medicare, Medicaid, Children's Health Insurance Program, and the Marketplace and maximize regulatory authorities to address inappropriate payments.

title: Modernizing the Commission's National Environmental Policy Act Rules
abstract: In this document (Order), the Federal Communications Commission ("Commission" or "FCC") takes action to cut through outdated and unnecessary burdens that have slowed deployment of critical communications networks. These reforms restore balance to the Commission's National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) implementation by providing clear and predictable rules to ensure NEPA serves as a tool for informed decision-making rather than a barrier to investment, innovation, and connectivity.

title: Appellate Procedures for the Board of Immigration Appeals
abstract: In February 2026, the Department issued an interim final rule ("IFR"), effective March 9, 2026, to streamline Board of Immigration Appeals ("Board" or "BIA") procedures. The IFR's comment period closed on April 8, 2026. In this final rule, the Department responds to comments received and finalizes the IFR with minor changes.

title: Marine Mammals; Proposed Incidental Harassment Authorization for the Southern Beaufort Sea Stock of Polar Bears During Exploration Activities in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge 1002 Area Alaska; Draft Environmental Assessment
abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, in response to a request under the Marine Mammal Protection Act from the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA), propose to authorize nonlethal incidental take by harassment of small numbers of Southern Beaufort Sea (SBS) polar bears (Ursus maritimus) for 1 year from the date of issuance of the incidental harassment authorization (IHA). The applicant requested this authorization for take by harassment that may result from activities associated with a seismic exploration program in the Coastal Plain of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge Section 1002 area. This proposed authorization, if finalized, will be take of polar bears associated with the specified activities, which may come from the SBS stock. We invite comments on the proposed IHA and accompanying draft environmental assessment from the public, Tribes, and local, State, and Federal agencies.

title: Certain Pea Protein From the People's Republic of China: Preliminary Results, Partial Rescission, and Preliminary Determination of No Shipments of Antidumping Duty Administrative Review; 2023-2025
abstract: The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) preliminarily determines that that certain producers/exporters subject to this review made sales of subject merchandise at less than normal value (NV) during the period of review (POR), November 15, 2023, through July 31, 2025. In addition, we are rescinding the review with respect to 26 companies. Interested parties are invited to comment on these preliminary results of review.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Dassault Aviation Airplanes
abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Dassault Aviation Model FALCON 6X airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a determination that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This proposed AD would require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Pesticide Registration Maintenance Fee; Cancellation Order for Certain Pesticide Registrations
abstract: Pursuant to the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or Agency) is hereby issuing an order for the cancellations of the pesticide product registrations identified in this document. EPA previously announced its receipt of and requested comments on requests to voluntarily cancel the product registrations listed in Table 1 of Unit II. and announced its intent to cancel the product registrations listed in Table 3 of Unit III. With the issuance of this cancellation order, any sale, distribution, or use of products listed in this notice will be permitted after the registrations have been cancelled only if such sale, distribution, or use is consistent with the terms as described in the final order.

title: Update to Statutory Citations and Internet Address in Bid Protest Regulations
abstract: The Government Accountability Office (GAO) is issuing a final rule to amend its Bid Protest Regulations, promulgated in accordance with the Competition in Contracting Act of 1984 (CICA), to make an administrative change by updating citations to the United States Code to reflect amendment and recodification of underlying statutory provisions. The revisions only reflect changes that update an internet address and that update statutory citations to reflect statutory changes, so GAO has determined that the rule is uncontroversial and therefore it is appropriate to issue a final rule.

title: Schedules of Controlled Substances: Placement of Oveporexton in Schedule IV
abstract: On August 5, 2026, the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a new drug application for Orzeyful (oveporexton) for the treatment of narcolepsy type 1 in adults. The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) provided the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) with a scheduling recommendation to place oveporexton, chemically known as N-[(2S,3R)-2-[[3-(3,5- difluorophenyl)-2-fluorophenyl]methyl]-4,4-difluoro-1-(2-hydroxy-2- methylpropanoyl)pyrrolidin-3-yl]ethanesulfonamide, in schedule IV of the Controlled Substances Act (CSA). In accordance with the CSA, as amended by the Improving Regulatory Transparency for New Medical Therapies Act, DEA is hereby issuing an interim final rule placing oveporexton, including its salts, isomers and salts of isomers whenever the existence of such salts, isomers, and salts of isomers is possible, in schedule IV of the CSA.

title: Pesticides; Notice of Receipt of Requests to Voluntarily Cancel Certain Pesticide Registrations and Amend Registrations To Terminate Certain Uses With a 30-Day Comment Period (September 2026)
abstract: This document announces the Agency's receipt of and solicits comments on requests by registrants to voluntarily cancel their pesticide registrations of certain products and to amend their product registrations to terminate one or more uses. In accordance with the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA), EPA provides a periodic notice of receipt addressing requests received by EPA since the last notice of receipt was issued and uses the month and year in the title to help distinguish one document from the other. EPA intends to grant these requests at the close of the comment period for this announcement unless the Agency receives substantive comments during the comment period that would merit further review of the requests or the requests are withdrawn by the registrant. If these requests are granted, EPA will issue an order in the Federal Register cancelling the listed product registrations, after which any sale, distribution, or use of the products listed in this document will only be permitted after the registrations have been cancelled if such sale, distribution, or use is consistent with the terms as described in the final order.

title: Agency Information Collection Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs Acquisition Regulation Provision 852.209-70
abstract: In compliance with the Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) of 1995, this notice announces that the Office of Procurement, Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), will submit the collection of information abstracted below to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and comment. The PRA submission describes the nature of the information and its expected cost and burden, and it includes the actual data collection instrument.

title: Housing and Community Development Act of 1980: Verification of Eligible Status
abstract: This final rule revises HUD's Section 214 regulations to require the verification of U.S. citizenship or the eligible immigration status of all applicants and recipients of assistance under a covered program regardless of age. The rule will also make prorated assistance a temporary condition pending verification of eligible status of all family members, where permitted by statute, as opposed to under HUD's current regulations where prorated assistance could continue indefinitely. These amendments bring HUD's regulations into greater alignment with the wording and purpose of Section 214 and align with the current Administration's priorities and regulatory reform efforts.

title: Modification of Significant New Uses of Certain Chemical Substances (23-1.M)
abstract: EPA is amending significant new use rules (SNURs) issued under section 5(a)(2) of the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for certain chemical substances identified herein, which were the subject of premanufacture notices (PMNs) and significant new use notices (SNUNs). This action amends the SNURs by allowing certain new uses reported in the SNUNs or PMNs without additional notification requirements, modifying the significant new use notification requirements based on the actions and determinations for the SNUN or PMN submissions or based on the examination of new test data or other information, and making technical amendments to several SNURs. EPA is issuing these amendments based on review of new and existing data for the chemical substances.

title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs; CY 2027 Payment Policies Under the Physician Fee Schedule and Other Changes to Part B Payment and Coverage Policies; Medicare Shared Savings Program Requirements; and Medicare Prescription Drug Inflation Rebate Program
abstract: This final rule addresses: changes to the physician fee schedule (PFS); other changes to Medicare Part B payment policies to ensure that payment systems are updated to reflect changes in medical practice, relative value of services, and changes in the statute; codification of establishment of new policies for: the Medicare Prescription Drug Inflation Rebate Program under the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022; limiting Medicare coverage of certain individuals; the Ambulatory Specialty Model; updates to drugs and biological products paid under Part B; Medicare Shared Savings Program requirements; updates to the Quality Payment Program; updates to policies for Rural Health Clinics and Federally Qualified Health Centers; update to the Ambulance Fee Schedule regulations; codification of the Inflation Reduction Act and Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 provisions; updates to Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule regulations; updates to the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program.

title: Medicare Program: Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment and Ambulatory Surgical Center Payment Systems; and Quality Reporting Programs; including the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program and Ambulatory Surgical Center Quality Program; Request for Information on Strengthening the Standardization and Comparability of Hospital Price Transparency (HPT) Data; Prior Authorization; Accrediting Organization (AO) Deeming for Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA); and Notices of Closure of Teaching Hospitals and Opportunities To Apply for Available Slots
abstract: This final rule with comment period revises the Medicare Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) and the Medicare Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) payment system for calendar year 2027 based on our continuing experience with these systems. We also describe the changes to the amounts and factors used to determine the payment rates for Medicare services paid under the OPPS and those paid under the ASC payment systems. In addition, this final rule with comment period updates and refines the requirements for the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program and the Ambulatory Surgical Center Quality Reporting Program. There are no changes to the Rural Emergency Hospital Quality Reporting Program. We finalized the expansion of the prior authorization requirement to include additional Botulinum Toxin Injection services. We also finalized implementation of certain provisions of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, for off-campus outpatient departments of a provider. In addition, this final rule with comment period announces notices of closure of teaching hospitals and opportunities to apply for available slots. Additionally, we finalized the policy that hospital accrediting organizations (AOs) with deeming authority may assess compliance with certain Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA) administrative requirements under 42 CFR 489.20 during accreditation and reaccreditation surveys.

abstract: This final rule focuses on deregulatory actions identified in HHS regulations regarding health information technology standards, implementation specifications, and certification criteria and regarding certification programs for health information technology. abstract: The DoD (referred to herein as "the Department of War" or "DoW") is publishing this notice to announce it is establishing the Advisory Council on Health and Human Performance Optimization ("the Council") as a discretionary Federal advisory committee.

title: Order Renewing Order Temporarily Denying Export Privileges
Outbound Investment Security Program Regulations
abstract: This proposed rule sets forth regulations that would implement Subtitle C of the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act, which is codified at Title VIII of the Defense Production Act. The proposed rule would require United States persons to provide notification to the U.S. Department of the Treasury regarding certain transactions involving foreign persons that are engaged in notifiable technologies; and prohibit United States persons from engaging in certain other transactions involving foreign persons that are engaged in prohibited technologies. Where consistent with Title VIII, the proposed rule incorporates certain definitions and concepts from the current regulations governing the Outbound Investment Security Program. The proposed rule also would add applicability dates to the regulations, such that those regulations would continue to apply to activities that occurred within the relevant timeframe.

title: Notice of Agreements Filed
Request for Information for 2028 Department of Defense (DoD) State Priorities Impacting Service Members and Their Families
abstract: On Tuesday, March 24, 2026, the Department of Defense (referred to herein as "the Department", "Department of War" or DoW") published a request for information in the Federal Register (FR) that provided an opportunity for the public to submit issues that have an impact on service members and their families, where state governments are the primary agents for making positive change. Each year, DoW selects state policy priorities for states to consider that represent barriers resulting from the transience and uncertainty of military life. For example, DoW has asked states to consider remedies that trade residency-based and time-in-state requirements for portability and continuity, including interstate compacts, license reciprocity, credit for military training, spouse unemployment compensation; cross- reporting agreements with child welfare agencies; educational opportunities including advance enrollment, homeschool solutions, in- state tuition, records transfer, and waiver waitlist retention for families with special needs; support for severely injured personnel; custody and juvenile justice protections for deployed parents and military-connected youth; information sharing on military protective orders; employment and legal protections for military families; and predatory lending safeguards. DoW will consider public submissions in setting those priorities.

title: Proposal of Special Measure Prohibiting the Transmittal of Funds Regarding Transactions Involving the A7 Network's Sub-Agents
abstract: FinCEN is issuing a finding and notice of proposed rulemaking, pursuant to section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act (Public Law 116-283), as amended by section 6106(b) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (Public Law 117-81), finding transactions involving any company operating outside of the United States that is controlled by the A7 Network, a sanctions evasion and money laundering service with ties to Russia, leveraged by a wide range of illicit actors, including Iran and its terrorist proxies, to be a class of transactions of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance and proposing the imposition of a prohibition on certain transmittals of funds, by any covered financial institution, involving that class of transactions.
